trident_get_schema.description:
Get the graph schema: what node types exist, what edge types connect them, counts,
and sample property names for each node type. Call this FIRST to understand the
structure of the knowledge graph before querying it.

trident_search.description:
Semantic search across graph nodes. Find entities, concepts, procedures, or steps by meaning.
Returns matching nodes with their node_id (use node_id with trident_get_node and trident_traverse).

node_type.description: Filter by node type: Entity, Concept, Procedure, Step. Leave empty for all.

trident_find_exact.description:
Find a node by its exact label or name (case-insensitive). Use this when you know
the specific name of an entity, concept, or procedure — faster and more precise than
semantic search. Returns the node with its Neo4j ID.

name.description: Exact entity/concept/procedure name to look up

node_type.description: Optional: Entity, Concept, Procedure, Step, Document, Chunk

trident_cypher.description:
Run a read-only Cypher query directly against Neo4j. This is the most powerful
tool — use it for complex multi-hop queries, pattern matching, aggregations, and
path finding that can't be done with simpler tools.

The query MUST include {provider_id: $provider_id} to scope to the active provider.
A LIMIT is auto-appended if not present.

Example queries:
- Find all entities connected to a procedure's steps:
  MATCH (p:Procedure {provider_id: $provider_id})-[:HAS_STEP]->(s:Step)-[:REFERENCES]->(e:Entity)
  RETURN p.name, s.step_number, s.description, e.label

- Find shortest path between two entities:
  MATCH (a:Entity {label: 'X', provider_id: $provider_id}),
        (b:Entity {label: 'Y', provider_id: $provider_id}),
        path = shortestPath((a)-[*..5]-(b))
  RETURN [n IN nodes(path) | labels(n)[0] + ': ' + coalesce(n.label, n.name, '')] AS path

- Count edges by type:
  MATCH (a {provider_id: $provider_id})-[r]->(b {provider_id: $provider_id})
  RETURN type(r) AS edge_type, count(r) AS count ORDER BY count DESC

query.description: Cypher query. MUST use {provider_id: $provider_id} filter. Read-only — no CREATE/DELETE/MERGE.

trident_get_node.description:
Get a specific node's properties and its meaningful connections.
By default, Chunk neighbours are excluded (use trident_get_chunks for text).
Shows Entity, Concept, Procedure, Step, Proposition, and Document connections.
Raise depth to explore multiple hops out in one call instead of chaining several
trident_get_node/trident_traverse calls -- depth>1 responses include an `edges`
list covering the whole multi-hop subgraph (see GraphStore.get_node_detail).

include_chunks.description: Include Chunk neighbours (noisy — usually skip). Default false.

depth.description: Max hops from this node to explore (1-5). Default 1 (direct neighbours only).

trident_traverse.description:
Walk the graph from a node. Follow specific edge types and filter by node types.
Use this to explore procedure DAGs, entity relationships, or concept hierarchies.

edge_types.description: Comma-separated edge types to follow, e.g. 'HAS_STEP,PRECEDES'. Empty for all.

node_types.description: Comma-separated node types to return, e.g. 'Step,Entity'. Empty for all.

trident_get_chunks.description:
Semantic search over raw document text. Returns the actual content from ingested documents.
Use this to find specific facts, clauses, or details not captured as graph nodes.

trident_get_procedures.description:
Get structured procedures (SOPs) with ordered steps.
Each procedure has a name, intent, and numbered steps with prerequisites.

query.description: Search by intent. Leave empty to list all procedures.

trident_get_stats.description:
Get a quick overview of what's in a provider's graph.
Shows counts of nodes, chunks, entities, concepts, propositions, procedures, plus
`counts_by_label` for every node label actually present, `provider_kind`, and
`has_ticket_store`. When `has_ticket_store` is true there is also a `ticket_mining`
block with the ticket counts, the label fields it can predict, and its measured
label-quality and accuracy figures — use trident_label_ticket to predict against it.
A provider can hold both knowledge data and tickets, so the graph counts and the
ticket block appear together rather than one instead of the other.

trident_label_ticket.description:
Predict label values for a support ticket, for providers with a ticket store.

Finds the most similar already-labelled tickets and ranks what THEY are labelled,
returning the top candidates per field with a confidence, how many neighbours backed
each one, and an example neighbour. Use trident_get_stats first to check the provider
has a ticket store and to see which label fields it has.

Kept as its own tool after `/label` folded into `trident_query`, because
`trident_query` is registered directly on the MCP server and is NOT in
`ALL_TOOLS` -- removing this one would take ticket labelling away from the
in-process LangGraph agent entirely, not just from the MCP surface. It is a
thin delegate over the same `label_tickets` core.

ticket.description: The ticket as a JSON object, shaped like a row of the dump the provider was ingested from

fields.description: Comma-separated label fields to predict. Leave empty for all of the provider's declared fields.

trident_episodes.description:
Inspect a provider's episodes: past situations, either lived or mined.

An episode is a record of a past situation. A **lived** episode is something
that actually happened once. A **mined** episode is a recurring pattern a
fitter detected across many records, carrying a confidence, a recurrence
count, and the examples it was drawn from.

Three modes, picked by which arguments you pass:
  - `episode_id` set: fetch exactly that episode, in full.
  - `query` set: find the episodes whose summaries are closest to that
    situation, with their similarity scores.
  - neither set: report what the episode store holds for this provider --
    whether it exists, how many episodes, and whether its embedding space
    matches this service's. Use this first when a `query` returns nothing,
    because "no relevant episodes" and "the store is misconfigured" look
    identical from the outside otherwise.

This is a read-only inspection tool and is deliberately separate from
`trident_query`, which recalls episodes automatically and folds them into
its answer. Use this one to see the episodes themselves.

query.description: Describe a situation to find past episodes like it. Leave empty to inspect the store instead.

episode_id.description: Fetch one specific episode by id. Overrides `query`.

top_k.description: How many episodes to return for a `query` (1-20).

include_events.description: Include each episode's full event log. Long — usually skip.

trident_create_entity.description:
Create a new entity in the knowledge graph.
The entity will be semantically indexed for future search and resolution.

trident_create_concept.description: Create a new concept (definition/term) in the knowledge graph.

trident_create_relationship.description:
Create a relationship (edge) between two existing entities or concepts.
Both source and target must already exist. Use edge types from the vocabulary:
RELATED_TO, PART_OF, INSTANCE_OF, GOVERNED_BY, LOCATED_IN, DEPENDS_ON, OPERATES,
USES, ACQUIRED_BY, CONNECTS_TO, MANAGES, TERMINATES_AT, PROVISIONED_FROM,
IMPLEMENTED_BY, DESCRIBED_BY, SOURCED_FROM, FLAGS, SUPERSEDES, BILLED_ON,
RECONCILES_TO, CLASSIFIED_AS, OTHER. Provide a brief description for context.

trident_query.description:
Run a retrieval-augmented query against a provider's knowledge base.

Returns a grounded answer with confidence score, source chunks, retrieved
procedures, graph provenance metadata, and -- when the provider has a ticket
store -- per-label confidences with example tickets. Knowledge, procedural
and graph retrieval always run together except under `ticket_mode="only"`;
they are three legs of one grounded answer and are not independently
selectable.

graph_hops.description:
BFS depth from matched entities. Omit to let the retrieved
question's classified intent pick a depth (roadmap 6.2) -- a
causal or exploratory question gets more hops than a direct
lookup. Pass an explicit value to override that entirely.

ticket_mode.description:
Whether the ticket store takes part in this query -- the
only optional store.
  "auto" (default): run the ticket leg when the provider has a
    usable ticket store. A provider with no ticket data is never
    an error, only a reason in `stores_skipped["ticket"]`.
  "off": never run the ticket leg. Incompatible with supplying
    `tickets` or `label_fields` -- that combination is a tool
    error, not silently ignored.
  "only": run ONLY the ticket leg -- no question embedding, no
    graph traversal, no LLM call. `answer` then points at
    `ticket_labels` rather than being prose.

tickets.description:
Structured ticket rows to label, shaped like rows of the dump
the provider was ingested from. At most 50. Results are index-aligned
in `ticket_labels`, and a row that could not be labelled carries
`ticket_labels[i].error` while the rest still succeed. Omit to label
the `question` text itself.

label_fields.description:
Restrict prediction to some of the provider's declared
label fields. Naming an undeclared field is an error, not a filter.

trident_feedback.description: Record feedback for a query or a specific task.

trident_ingest.description:
Ingest external content into a provider's knowledge base via the intake service.

Supports three connector types (set `connector_type`):

- "content": Ingest inline text or JSON passed directly. Requires `content`.
             The intake service ingests files, not raw strings, so the
             content is wrapped as an in-memory document and uploaded via the
             file connector. Optional `filename` (extension decides parsing;
             auto-detected as .json/.txt when omitted). Max 50 MB.
- "url":     Fetch a single file from an HTTP/HTTPS URL. Requires `url`.
- "scraper": Scrape one or more web pages. Requires `urls` (comma-separated).
             Optional: `crawl_depth` (0-2), `respect_robots`, `merge_pages`
             (when true, all crawled pages become one document/job).
- "rest_api": Call a REST endpoint and ingest the response. Requires `rest_url`.
             Optional: `rest_method` (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE),
             `rest_headers` / `rest_params` (JSON object strings),
             `rest_body` (raw string), `rest_auth_type`
             (none|bearer|basic|api_key) with `rest_auth_value` /
             `rest_auth_username` / `rest_api_key_header`,
             `rest_timeout`, `rest_verify_ssl`.
- "database": Query a DB table/collection. Requires `db_type`
             (postgres|mysql|mongodb), `database`, and `table_name`
             (collection name for mongodb). Connection:
             - postgres: `pg_connection_string` OR `host`+`db_username`+`db_password`
             - mysql:    `host`+`db_username`+`db_password`
             - mongodb:  `mongo_connection_uri` OR `host` (+`mongo_auth_source`,
                         `mongo_tls`)
             Optional: `port`, `columns` (comma-separated), `date_column`
             + `date_from` + `date_to`, `row_limit`.
- "jira":    Fetch issues + attachments from a Jira Cloud project. Requires
             `base_url`, `email`, `api_token`, `project_key`. Optional:
             `max_results`.

Common options: `document_type` (text|sop|tabular), `provider_name`,
TTL controls (`has_ttl`, `ttl_days`), and graph extraction:
  - `extraction_mode` (comprehensive|balanced|precise) — REQUIRED for the
    knowledge graph to be built. Defaults to "comprehensive"; set to "" to
    skip extraction (chunks/vectors only, no graph).
  - `entity_types` / `relationship_types` — optional JSON-string definitions
    to constrain extraction.
  - `chunking_type`, `chunk_size`, `chunk_overlap` — optional chunking
    overrides; the service default is used when left unset.

Ingestion is asynchronous: this returns immediately with a `req_id` (and,
for scraper, a per-URL accepted/failures breakdown) once the request is
accepted — it does not mean processing is complete.
